description: The framework registry for endpoint, service and URL detection (P7). The detector matches RESOLVED annotation FQNs, DSL callee FQNs and supertype names against these patterns (suffix-segment match, see PatternMatcher) and never hard-codes a framework. A framework the pack does not name is invisible by construction, and every pattern here is validated by a build-time test. annotation FQNs must resolve through the workspace declarations or a real classpath: an unresolved annotation keeps its PSI short name and only matches when the pack pattern is itself a short name, which is never — type identity, not name matching, is what keeps a homonym annotation from becoming an endpoint.

frameworks._p15_comment: P15, corrected in P17: http4k's CORE DSL (`"/path" bind METHOD to handler`) has no media/auth declaration site - the handler is a plain function, content types live in lenses and responses. That half was and remains the truth. The P15 claim that contract meta {} is 'OpenAPI documentation, not routing' was WRONG for the security field: see _p17_comment.
frameworks._p17_comment: P17, sourced against the pinned corpus clone (github.com/http4k/http4k at b051f89d, release 6.59.0.0): the contract DSL has TWO real auth declaration sites, both applied at RUN TIME. (1) The contract block's own `security` - ContractBuilder.security: Security? (core/api/openapi/src/main/kotlin/org/http4k/contract/extensions.kt:33), read by ContractRouteMatcher.kt:46 for every route in the block. (2) A route's meta lambda - RouteMetaDsl.security: Security? (routeMeta.kt:52) carried by RouteMeta.security: Security? (routeMeta.kt:228), attached with `"/x" meta { security = .. } bindContract GET to h` (String.meta and String.bindContract, extensions.kt:61-63). Precedence is the framework's own elvis at ContractRouteMatcher.kt:121: `it.meta.security?.filter ?: security?.filter ?: Filter.NoOp` - per-route meta OVERRIDES the block. Scheme constructors (core/security/core/src/main/kotlin/org/http4k/security/): BasicAuthSecurity.kt:8, ApiKeySecurity.kt:19, BearerAuthSecurity.kt:10, MutualTLSSecurity.kt:10, OpenIdConnectSecurity.kt:6 (NoSecurity is the absence of a requirement and is deliberately not modelled). P17 review: OAuthSecurity.kt:9 declares a SEALED class - it cannot be constructed, so modelling `org.http4k.security.OAuthSecurity` matched nothing and would never have fired. The constructible OAuth schemes are its five subclasses in the same file (AuthCodeOAuthSecurity:19, ImplicitOAuthSecurity:31, UserCredentialsOAuthSecurity:43, ClientCredentialsOAuthSecurity:65, DeviceCodeOAuthSecurity:87), and those are what is modelled. ContractRoute.kt:80 applies meta.security?.filter outside a contract block too. meta produces/consumes (routeMeta.kt:43-44) are NOT read by the matcher - they feed the OpenAPI renderer - so media on contract routes stays an honest empty.

frameworks._p15_comment: P15: the route builder's vararg RouteRole tail IS the auth requirement (get("/x", handler, Role.ADMIN)). Media has no declaration site in Javalin's DSL - ctx.contentType() is a response detail inside the handler, not a route declaration - so consumes/produces stay an honest empty.

P15: media has no declaration site for servlets - the content type is a response header the handler sets. Authentication IS declared, in the deployment descriptor's <security-constraint>, which the web.xml parser reads (P15) and attaches per url-pattern; it is not an annotation.
P15: media sits on the ROUTE OBJECT between the route call and the handler (router.get("/x").produces("application/json").handler { .. }) and is read from the chained calls.
frameworks._p17_comment: P17, closing the P15 honest-empty: Vert.x auth IS attributable to one route, because the requirement is attached THROUGH the same chained handler call the media ride - `route.handler(BasicAuthHandler.create(auth))`. Sourced from io.vertx:vertx-web:5.1.7 (the artifact in the corpus warm cache), class files read from the jar: io/vertx/ext/web/Route.class declares `handler(Handler<RoutingContext>)` returning Route (so the chain continues past an auth attach); io/vertx/ext/web/handler/AuthenticationHandler.class `extends Handler<RoutingContext>` - an auth handler IS a handler, no overload involved; the factories are interface statics on each handler class (BasicAuthHandler.create(AuthenticationProvider[, realm]), JWTAuthHandler.create(JWTAuth[, issuer]), DigestAuthHandler.create(Vertx, HtdigestAuth[, timeout]), OAuth2AuthHandler.create(Vertx, OAuth2Auth[, redirectUri]), OtpAuthHandler.create(TotpAuth|HotpAuth), RedirectAuthHandler.create(AuthenticationProvider[, loginRedirectURL]), WebAuthn4JHandler.create(WebAuthn4J)). P18 symbol-kind check (against the same 5.1.7 jar): the nesting entry was io.vertx.ext.web.Router.mountSubRouter - an API Vert.x 5 REMOVED (Router declares no mount* member; the 5.x spelling is Route.subRouter(Router), javap on io/vertx/ext/web/Route.class). The old entry named a symbol the cited evidence does not contain and was inert besides (no fixture exercises it and the prefix walk keys on route/path lambda links); it is replaced by the 5.x spelling. Vert.x sub-router PREFIX composition remains unmodelled for either spelling - a named gap, not a wrong answer. ChainAuthHandler.all()/any() and AuthorizationHandler.create() are deliberately not modelled: the former builds a composite with no single scheme to name, the latter is authorization (what may you do), not authentication (who are you). The P15 claim that the KIR cannot attribute the value was wrong for THIS shape: the factory call's own callee names the scheme.
